title: Neymar apologises to Robinho Jr after Santos training ground altercation
content:
Santos forward Neymar said he apologised to team-mate Robinho Jr over an altercation between the pair at the Brazilian club’s training ground.

Santos said in a statement widely-reported in local media that the club was investigating an incident between Robinho Jr, 18, and Neymar, 34, which occurred on Sunday at the Rei Pele Training Centre.

Robinho Jr, son of Neymar’s former Brazil teammate Robinho, told reporters on Monday that the incident had been settled.

Neymar scored Santos’ only goal as they drew 1-1 with Recoleta in the Copa Sudamericana group stage match on Tuesday, and embraced Robinho Jr, who was an unused substitute.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Neymar said the incident was due to a disagreement in training and that his reaction “went a little too far”, and that he apologised to Robinho Jr in front of the Santos squad, as well as to the teenager’s family.

“Right after it happened, we apologised; we talked in the locker room — both Robinho Jr and I — and we sorted things out there,” Neymar said in quotes carried by ESPN.

“He’s a kid I really like; I’ve had a special fondness for him from the start. This happens in soccer; you fight with a brother, with a friend. I’ve argued with several of my friends in soccer; I’ve fought with everyone, and that’s just how it goes.”

When asked if he would withdraw a complaint he was reported to have made, Robinho Jr said, via ESPN Brasil: “Yes. I accept the apology; it’s normal, everyone makes mistakes. I’m a human being like all of us; I could have made a mistake too, just as I’ve made many mistakes before.”

Robinho Jr added that the incident was “blown out of proportion”.

Neymar said he felt the situation was accentuated due to the spotlight on him in Brazil, and that everyone involved in the sport knows “fights, fist fights, slaps” can happen, describing it as “part of the game”.

Neymar returned to action in February after undergoing arthroscopy surgery on his knee in December. He has recorded five goals and three assists in 12 matches this term, and Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti said he must prove his fitness in order to be selected for next month’s World Cup squad.
